subject: botany_2
question_text: How many types of RNA polymerases exist in cells? Write their names and functions.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.33, printed question 40. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". insider_note: Three enzymes, three products. Write them as a three-row table if you can — it is faster and impossible to misread.

steps.label: How many, and where
steps.margin_note: The number, the location, and the bacterial contrast.
lines: In eukaryotic cells there are THREE types of
All three are found in the NUCLEUS.
Each one transcribes a different class of RNA.
(In bacteria a SINGLE RNA polymerase makes all
steps.why: Eukaryotes divide the work between three enzymes where a bacterium uses one, which is the point the question is checking.
common_mistakes: Saying there are three in bacteria. Bacteria have ONE; eukaryotes have three.
Saying they are in the cytoplasm. All three are in the NUCLEUS.
steps.memory_tip: Three in a eukaryote, one in a bacterium.

steps.label: RNA polymerase I
steps.margin_note: Name the three rRNAs with their S values. Three lines.
lines: RNA POLYMERASE I transcribes the ribosomal
These are the RNAs that build the ribosome.
steps.why: The three rRNAs it makes are needed in enormous quantity, which is why one enzyme is given over to them alone.
common_mistakes: Saying pol I makes mRNA. That is pol II.
Leaving out the S numbers. 28S, 18S and 5.8S are what the mark is for.
steps.memory_tip: Pol one makes the ribosome's own RNA.

steps.label: RNA polymerase II
steps.margin_note: Say precursor, expand hnRNA, and name the processing. Five lines.
lines: RNA POLYMERASE II transcribes the precursor of
mRNA, which is called heterogeneous nuclear RNA
hnRNA is then processed — capped, tailed and
steps.why: Pol II makes the RNA that will be translated into protein, which is why examiners ask about it more often than about the other two.
common_mistakes: Saying pol II makes mRNA directly. It makes hnRNA, the PRECURSOR of mRNA.
Not expanding hnRNA. Heterogeneous nuclear RNA is the full name.
steps.memory_tip: Pol two makes the message, but only a rough draft of it.

steps.label: RNA polymerase III
steps.margin_note: All three products, then one closing line. Watch 5S against 5.8S.

lines.text: I: rRNA · II: hnRNA · III: tRNA

lines: RNA POLYMERASE III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA
So the three enzymes between them make every
kind of RNA the cell needs.
steps.why: Between the three, every class of RNA is accounted for, which is the check that the answer is complete.
common_mistakes: Giving pol III the 5.8S rRNA. Pol III makes the 5S rRNA; 5.8S belongs to pol I.
Leaving out snRNA. It is one of pol III's named products.
steps.memory_tip: Pol three makes the small ones: tRNA, 5S and snRNA.
